name: Santander air-raid shelter (Refugio Antiaéreo)
story: Santander, then in the Republican zone, was bombed repeatedly during 1937, and over a hundred shelters were dug beneath the city. This one, under the Plaza del Príncipe (then Plaza de Mariana Pineda), was built in spring 1937. It has three connected galleries for about 70 people, mainly military commanders and city officials. It was abandoned after the war and buried during the rebuilding that followed the great fire of 1941. It was rediscovered in 2006 during works on the Plaza Porticada and opened as a museum in 2014. The city fell to Nationalist and Italian troops on 26 August 1937.
see: About 100 m of restored underground galleries with audiovisuals, period photographs and objects, a Condor Legion airman's equipment and a 250 kg bomb.
plan: Guided visits only, in small groups (about €3). Closed Mondays; book ahead by phone (942 203 099).
